description: CardSpoke Plugin API Capabilities - Complete reference for plugin developers and AI agents. Every JS-bearing plugin runs inside its own sandboxed Worker (CS-002, resolved): no document/window/localStorage/raw fetch, every ctx.api call is async, and UI is described with ctx.h(tag, props, children) instead of document.createElement.

permissions.name: ui-override
permissions.description: Modify the user interface and inject custom elements

permissions.name: storage
permissions.description: Access and modify local storage (namespaced per plugin)

permissions.name: data-modify
permissions.description: Create, update, and delete cards and tags

permissions.name: network
permissions.description: Make network requests to external services

permissions.name: filesystem
permissions.description: Access the file system (mobile platforms only)

permissions.name: core-override
permissions.description: Override core application functions (very high risk)
requiredFor: middleware operations that modify core behavior

methods.name: inject
methods.description: Build real DOM from a vnode (ctx.h(...)) and inject it at a specified selector. There is no DOM inside the plugin's sandboxed worker, so a vnode description crosses instead of a real HTMLElement.
methods.signature: inject(selector: string, vnode: Vnode, position?: 'before'|'after'|'prepend'|'append'): Promise<{ remove(): Promise<void>, update(vnode: Vnode): Promise<void> }>

args.name: vnode
args.description: ctx.h(tag, props, children) description of the element to inject

args.name: position
args.description: Where to inject relative to target

methods.returns: Promise resolving to a handle: remove() undoes the injection, update(vnode) replaces its attrs/children in place

methods.name: replace
methods.description: Replace an element in the DOM with one built from a vnode
methods.signature: replace(selector: string, vnode: Vnode): Promise<{ remove(): Promise<void>, update(vnode: Vnode): Promise<void> }>

args.name: selector
args.description: CSS selector for element to replace

args.name: vnode
args.description: ctx.h(tag, props, children) description of the replacement element

methods.returns: Promise resolving to a handle (same shape as inject); the original is restored on remove()/cleanup

methods.name: registerComponent
methods.description: Register a custom component that can override default rendering. render(props) returns a vnode (may be async), not an HTMLElement.
methods.signature: registerComponent(name: string, component: { render(props): Vnode | Promise<Vnode>, priority?: number }): Promise<void>

args.name: component
args.description: Component object with render method (returns a vnode) and priority

methods.returns: Promise<void>
methods.example: await ctx.api.ui.registerComponent('Card', { render: (props) => ctx.h('div', {}, props.card.title), priority: 10 })

methods.name: unregisterComponent
methods.returns: Promise<void>

methods.name: showToast
methods.description: Show a toast notification to the user
methods.signature: showToast(message: string, type?: 'info'|'success'|'warning'|'error', duration?: number): Promise<void>
methods.returns: Promise<void>

middleware.description: Middleware operations that can be intercepted by plugins

operations.name: card.render
operations.description: A batched decorator, not a (mwCtx, next) middleware — fires once per tile per render batch, with NO live DOM element and NO next()/stopPropagation(). Registered the same way (ctx.api.middleware.register({operations:['card.render'], handler})) but handler(card, tileSnapshot) returns a patch object instead. See docs/architecture/PLUGIN_SYSTEM.md 'The card.render decorator contract'.
operations.handlerReturns: { addClass?, removeClass?, setStyle?, setStyleByIndex?, appendChildren?, prependChildren? } | null
operations.example: handler: async (card, tileSnapshot) => tileSnapshot.hasTags ? { addClass: ['tagged'] } : null

operations.name: card.save
operations.description: Called when a card is saved
operations.example: Middleware can validate data or add computed fields

operations.name: card.delete
operations.description: Called when a card is deleted
operations.example: Middleware can show confirmation or prevent deletion

operations.name: card.create
operations.description: Called when a card is created
operations.example: Middleware can set defaults or validate input

operations.name: card.update
operations.description: Called when a card is updated
operations.example: Middleware can validate changes or track history

usage.example: window.CardSpoke.Middleware.register({name: 'my-middleware', priority: 10, operations: ['card.save'], handler: async (ctx, next) => { await next(); }})

available.name: Card
available.description: Individual card tile, resolved via a batched RPC round trip into the plugin's worker once per render pass. render(props) returns a vnode (ctx.h(...)), may be async, and races a short deadline — a slow/hung render falls back to the default tile for that pass.
available.priority: Higher priority components override lower priority ones

available.name: Sidebar
available.priority: Higher priority components override lower priority ones

usage.register: await ctx.api.ui.registerComponent(name, {render: (props) => Vnode | Promise<Vnode>, priority: number})

selectors.description: Stable DOM selectors for plugin UI manipulation. Use data-plugin-anchor attributes for stable targeting that survives layout refactors.

semantic-anchors.description: Stable data-plugin-anchor attributes on key UI elements. Use [data-plugin-anchor='name'] as CSS/JS selector.

best-practices: Use IDs when available as fallback
Avoid relying on classes that may change

validation.description: Plugin content is validated before registration. Invalid plugins are rejected.
manifest-rules: manifest.permissions must be array of valid permission names
css-rules: Dangerous patterns are removed: @import, javascript:, behavior:, -moz-binding, expression()
js-rules: eval() and new Function() are not allowed

context.description: Plugin context object (ctx) provided to setup() and teardown()

h.description: ctx.h(tag, props, children) — build a vnode; there is no document.createElement inside the sandboxed worker

api.description: API object with ui, data, storage, and events

best-practices: Errors in teardown should not crash app

notes: Every JS-bearing plugin runs inside its own dedicated Web Worker (CS-002, resolved) — no document, window, localStorage, or raw fetch/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket/indexedDB/caches
Permissions are enforced by the sandbox's construction, not just checked at API boundaries — a denied permission is unreachable, not merely discouraged
Storage is namespaced per plugin (prefix: 'plugin_{id}_') and that namespace is a real boundary now, not just a naming convention
A hung setup() (or a genuine infinite loop) is time-boxed and its worker is forcibly terminated — it cannot freeze the app
All setup errors trigger automatic cleanup
Teardown errors are logged but don't stop app
best-practices: Validate user input before creating/updating cards
Handle errors gracefully in async operations (every ctx.api call is a Promise)
Test teardown thoroughly to avoid memory leaks
Document all permissions in manifest description

ui-injection.description: Inject an element into the UI (there is no document inside the sandbox — build a vnode with ctx.h instead)
